title: map.json
description: Decision-point graph and claim list for one artifact version. Rewritten by review-run each round.

summary.description: One-sentence statement of the artifact's main conclusion, for orientation.

leads.description: Detective leads: anomalies, untested implications, unexcluded rival explanations, places where a model stands in for design, parts that do not cohere. Shown to the person as highlighted questions; never fixed by the AI.

assessments.description: The reviewer's judgement of each aspect of the artifact: how good it is, why, and what is worth the person's thought. One entry per aspect in plan.aspects.

readiness.description: The AI reviewer's verdict before the person reads: is the work ready for their review, or should its author (often another agent) do more first?

text.description: Two or three sentences: why, in plain academic prose.

tasks.description: What the author should do: before the person's review when revise_first; when ready (or when the author cannot be reached), what they should still improve.

sent_to.description: Where the task list was sent, if it was (an agent or session name).

overview.description: The review's top layer: the work's architecture, in the parts its type defines (TYPE.md `overview`), and the questions that decide whether it stands. In-text notes deal with details only.

name.description: The part's heading, from the type (e.g. 研究叙事, 产品主张).

text.description: A short paragraph in plain academic prose (skills/WRITING.md).

refs.description: Ids of in-text notes that bear on this part.

path.description: Plans only (TYPE.md `work: plan`): the suggested way forward — what to do first, what to cut, the cheapest test — as ordered steps. Such advice lives here once, not inside problem notes.

text.description: One or two sentences: the idea behind the suggested order.

key_questions.description: The few questions that decide whether the work stands; the only things the author must weigh.

kind.description: Which kinds a type uses is set by TYPE.md `lead_kinds`. For plans: untested_assumption: the plan rests on something not yet checked. open_choice: a choice the plan has not made but must. missing_piece: something the plan needs and has not thought about. For research: anomaly: a result that does not fit the main claim. untested_implication: something the claim predicts that was never checked. rival_explanation: another account of the main result not yet ruled out. model_for_design: a model carries a conclusion that the design itself does not establish. incoherence: parts of the argument that do not fit together.

observation.description: What the artifact or its materials show, plainly.

threat.description: Why this could weaken or overturn the main claim if it is what it looks like.

questions.description: Questions for the person: what to look at, what evidence would settle it. No answer is assumed.

rating.description: Finished work (TYPE.md `work: finished`, the default) — strong: an expert would accept it as is. adequate: sound, with fixable problems. weak: a problem here undermines the work. Plans (`work: plan`) — clear: thought through. partial: has a direction, not yet worked out. open: not yet addressed.

reasons.description: Why, each tied to the artifact; strengths as well as problems.

questions.description: Important questions this aspect raises that the person should think about; no answer is assumed.

decision.description: A decision point in QOC-E form: Question, Options, Criteria, Evidence.

options.description: Exactly one option has chosen=true (checked by the validator, not expressible cleanly here).

stated_in_artifact.description: false when the criterion is inferred by the AI rather than written by the author.

upstream.description: Decisions this one depends on. If one of them changes, this one becomes invalidated.

downstream.description: Inverse of upstream; the validator checks the two agree.

score.description: 0 none; 1 local wording; 2 changes a specific result; 3 changes the main conclusion.

basis.description: sensitivity: an alternative was actually re-run. dependency: many downstream nodes. judgement: AI estimate only.

status.description: ai_default: not load-bearing, AI keeps the author's choice and lists it at sign-off. invalidated: an upstream decision changed after this was confirmed.

prompt_to_human.description: The exact question shown to the person when human_action is answer or predict.

challenge.description: Optional short counter-argument from the AI, shown as an ignorable margin note.

sensitivity.description: What happens to the conclusion if this option is used instead. Only present when actually computed or reasoned with evidence.

computed.description: true only if the alternative was actually re-run; evidence must then include the command.

source_type.description: computed: from data. literature: cited work. user_stated: the person said it. model_inference: reasoning by the model. unsourced: no source found; listed separately.

check_status.description: verified needs at least one source; 'checked, no problem' is shown explicitly.
